title: DEFAULT values
description: ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET DEFAULT gives a column a fallback value used whenever a future INSERT doesn't specify one - it doesn't touch rows that already exist. Set the DEFAULT for `customers.country` to `'Unknown'`.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: SET DEFAULT
The pattern mirrors SET NOT NULL from an earlier exercise: ALTER TABLE <table> ALTER COLUMN <column> SET DEFAULT <value> - the value needs quotes here since country is a text column.
Target the customers table's country column, and set its default to the text 'Unknown' (with quotes, since it's a text column).
expected_behavior: Future INSERTs into customers that omit country get 'Unknown' automatically; existing rows are unaffected.
solution: ALTER TABLE customers ALTER COLUMN country SET DEFAULT 'Unknown';
explanation: A DEFAULT only fires at INSERT time for a row that leaves the column out entirely - it's not the same as a CHECK constraint or a NOT NULL rule, and it does nothing at all to rows already in the table.
